A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MemVR research. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial reorganization and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original MemVR benchmark evaluations, static-versus-dynamic injection experiments, injection-ratio analysis, noise sensitivity tests, and qualitative cases.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds HallusionBench evaluations, modality interventions, threshold experiments, an adaptive-ratio variant, and LLaVA-Next results.

M1.justification: The core FFN visual retracing and entropy-triggered injection procedure remains. v2 adds the optional MemVR† variant, which computes the injection ratio as alpha = 2(u - gamma) instead of using a fixed ratio (Section 5.4, Table 9). The rewritten formulation using already aligned visual tokens does not establish a separate change to the core procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds HallusionBench, extending evaluation to its diagnostic hallucination and visual-illusion questions (Table 5). The seven existing benchmarks remain represented. This expands coverage within image-based multimodal evaluation; the discussed audio and other modalities are future proposals, not evaluated tasks.

E2.justification: v1 primarily compares against VCD and OPERA. v2 adds numerical ICD comparisons across retained hallucination, general-performance, and efficiency experiments, including the appendix tables. Conversely, the numerical Qwen-VL OPERA comparisons on the MME hallucination subset in v1 Table 3 are absent from v2 Table 8.

E3.justification: v2 substantially extends the evaluation design with three LLaVA-Next configurations, HallusionBench metrics and GPT-4o-mini judging, and latency, throughput, and memory measurements. It also changes the reported MME hallucination-subset total from five components including commonsense reasoning to four object/attribute components (v1 Table 3 versus v2 Table 8). The retained benchmarks' basic decoding settings largely remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds text-versus-image feature scaling and text/image/combined reinjection controls (Figure 4), a hallucinated-fruit uncertainty case (Figure 5), threshold sensitivity, and adaptive-ratio comparisons (Figure 7, Table 9). Injection-ratio and static-versus-dynamic analyses are retained in revised displays. The Gaussian-noise robustness experiment in v1 Figure 7 and Section 4.2 is removed.

E5.justification: v2 Figure 6 introduces error bars and box/violin summaries for LLaVA-Bench variability, although their statistical definitions are unspecified. Both reproducibility appendices already describe three differently seeded image samples and mean/standard-deviation calculation. The new displays therefore change reporting without establishing an increase in runs or a new significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: Numerous results are added or revised. For COCO-POPE average accuracy, LLaVA changes from 81.38 to 79.83 and MemVR from 87.00 to 86.93 (v1 Table 2; v2 Table 4). v2 adds sampling-specific POPE scores, ICD, HallusionBench, adaptive-ratio, resource-use, and LLaVA-Next results, while removing Qwen-VL POPE results. MME comparisons also change substantially; these revisions do not establish same-setting method improvements.

T1.justification: The mutual-information, conditional-entropy, and information-bottleneck theorems and proofs are substantively retained from v1 Section 3.5/Appendix B to v2 Section 4.4/Appendix A. The standalone LUFH assumption label disappears, but its underlying uncertainty–hallucination premise remains. Expanded FFN algebra and standard CHAIR formulas explain existing mathematics rather than introduce new theoretical results.

C1.justification: The training-free retracing and performance claims remain, but v2 elevates text-decoder sensitivity and modality imbalance from v1's proposed explanation to an explicitly experimentally validated principal contribution. Its abstract and introduction consequently claim a stronger diagnosis of hallucination causes, and its positioning asserts that MemVR uniquely combines hallucination mitigation with general improvement.

C2.justification: v2 develops the explanation that autoregressive generation increasingly favors textual information and interprets modality interventions as supporting visual-memory refresh. Section 5.6 adds two failure mechanisms: disrupting otherwise correct reasoning and failing because of image complexity or existing knowledge gaps. It also discusses excessive injection, while removing v1's explicit interpretation of sensitivity to noisy visual features.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies LLaVA candidate-layer buckets [0,15) and [15,31), MME-based bucket selection with 2–4 validation trials, and the HallusionBench evaluator. Most decoding hyperparameters and the GPU inventory are retained. The disclosure about using published VCD scores narrows from POPE/MME to POPE. These documentation changes do not by themselves establish that existing experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands research positioning through a dedicated comparison table and discussion distinguishing attention intervention, contrastive decoding, and hidden-state retracing. Newly discussed works include ICD, HALC, SID, VORD, EAH, CCA, and PAI. This changes the substantive comparison framework beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contributions, and method exposition are extensively rewritten. v1's combined methodology section becomes separate Background and Motivation and Methodology sections, and the question-organized experiments become dedicated results, ablation, latency, and case-study sections. Appendix ethics discussion is condensed into an Impact Statement.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column main-text layout, redraws the method diagram and uncertainty heatmaps, adds modality and distribution plots, and extensively restructures comparison tables. POPE gains sampling-specific columns, and several original figures disappear or are replaced. Many appendix case studies and the token-length timing table are retained but relocated.

improvement.justification: The modality controls, threshold experiments, and explicit failure analysis improve the evidential support and applicability discussion beyond v1's largely hypothesis-driven account. Broader comparator and backbone evaluations also make the claims more testable. These gains are limited by removal of the noise-robustness test, unexplained score revisions, and claims that exceed the reported evidence: for example, v2 Table A1 gives Qwen-VL ICD an MME score of 1833.75 versus MemVR's 1820.95 despite broad superiority language. The net quality gain is useful but limited.
